subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept native backup exclude controls in core now, and what restore-safe semantics should be required for ignore files, protected paths, external assets, and large-archive validation?
rationale: The feature is useful and linked to canonical backup issues, but exclusion defaults and implicit local files decide whether backups stay restorable and whether sensitive files are included or omitted.

options.title: Require a safe rework before merge
options.body: Continue with this PR only after it rebases onto current main, removes implicit `.backupignore` behavior or makes it explicit, applies excludes to every asset root or fails loudly, avoids full create-time archive scans, and includes real proof.

options.title: Narrow to explicit custom excludes
options.body: Accept a smaller first step with only explicit `--exclude` and `--exclude-file`, while deferring smart defaults and automatic ignore files until restore semantics are settled.

options.title: Pause or replace the branch
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and ask for a fresh smaller PR if preserving current main’s backup architecture makes this branch too costly to rescue.

recommendation.title: Require a safe rework before merge
recommendation.body: Continue with this PR only after it rebases onto current main, removes implicit `.backupignore` behavior or makes it explicit, applies excludes to every asset root or fails loudly, avoids full create-time archive scans, and includes real proof.
